clue.text: After former affair, wife to settle up individually? (7, two words)

indicators.note: the clue's first word sets the order: the spouse word is placed behind the affair word

blocks.note: an archaic sense of go is an affair or business, as in 'a rum go'
Cockney slang: 'my old dutch' is my wife

explanation.surface: A man whose old fling is over now wants his wife to pay her own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' for wife comes from Cockney slang (duchess of Fife). 'Former' flags that this sense of the short verb is dated.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each diner paying their own share of the bill.

clue.text: A person knowledgeable about diet

blocks.note: surface reading: the plain dictionary meaning, an expert on eating
setter's reading: this is the puzzle's competition entry, which solvers were invited to clue themselves, so no wordplay is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was Azed's clue-writing competition word: the printed clue is only the definition, and solvers had to supply their own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Built from Greek gaster (belly) and sophos (wise), the word names someone skilled in the science of good eating.

clue.text: Head of SA clan maybe publishing firm answer

explanation.surface: A publisher's reply about the leader of a Scottish clan.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is South Africa, not a Scottish clan: Afrikaans speakers call a grandfather oupa.
explanation.definitionFit: In South African English a grandfather, the patriarch at the top of a family, is called an oupa.

clue.text: With pretty girl around there's start of hurrying in pulse

indicators.note: the girl word goes around, enclosing the other piece
the beginning of the next word is all that is kept

blocks.note: a doll is a pretty girl

explanation.surface: Someone in a rush feels their pulse race with an attractive girl nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but means an edible seed such as a lentil; dholl is a variant spelling of dal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dholl is split lentils or peas, and lentils and peas are leguminous seeds known as pulses.

clue.text: Lectures to follow carefully, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved round to the end of the word

blocks.note: to stalk is to follow stealthily

explanation.surface: Lectures one ought to follow closely, from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the S of STALK to the back gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Talks given to an audience are lectures, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Cowboy's charge? First for him, leading cavalier

indicators.note: going before, so the single letter comes in front of the horseman
'him' points back to the cowboy, and only his initial is wanted

blocks.note: the cowboy word does double duty, also giving its initial
a ritter is a knight or horseman (from German)

explanation.surface: A cowboy is charged with something, and a gallant horseman leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' is something in one's care, not an accusation or a cavalry charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Critter is US dialect for a creature, especially a head of cattle, the animals a cowboy tends.

clue.text: Refrain's line, introduced by a harp's tremolo

definitions.note: a possessive noun standing for an adjective: of a phrase

indicators.note: a tremolo is a trembling, wavering sound, so the letters quiver into a new order
preceded by: the single letter comes after the other piece

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A song's chorus line is preceded by a wavering note on the harp.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is a musical phrase, and phrasal means belonging to or consisting of a phrase.

clue.text: Deal e.g. supplying east with ace in game

indicators.note: the game word is supplied with the other letters inside it

explanation.surface: A card deal that gives one player the ace in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is not a hand of cards but a town on the Kent coast, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is a coastal town with a harbour history, an example of a port town.

clue.text: Consort of Queen Empress, maybe, champion of old

blocks.note: the king partners the queen in cards and chess

explanation.surface: Who was the husband of Queen Victoria, Empress of India, as a champion of former times?
explanation.definitionFit: Kemp is an archaic word for a warrior or champion fighter.

clue.text: It's year ending in crisp, shivery, bitter cold

indicators.note: shivering letters shake out of their order
only the final letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: The year ends crisp and shivery in bitter cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness, and the term is used of severe weather, such as a biting frost.

clue.text: Has forgotten king in layout with fellows in club

indicators.note: the ruler's letter sits inside the layout word

blocks.note: mise is a setting or arrangement, as in mise en scène
a club's fellows are its members

explanation.surface: A king has forgotten where the club fellows were seated in the layout.
explanation.definitionFit: To misremember is to recall wrongly, effectively to have forgotten the correct version.

clue.text: Pairs falling out about endless effrontery in board game

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter goes
pairs that fall out split up and scatter into a new order
around: the scrambled letters surround the other piece

explanation.surface: Couples fall out over someone's cheek during a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcheesi is a trademarked American board game derived from the Indian game pachisi.

clue.text: One's clumsy in company, breaking end off fine china

definitions.note: read as 'one who's clumsy in company', a noun phrase

indicators.note: the final letter is snapped off the china word

blocks.note: Spode is a famous English porcelain maker

explanation.surface: A clumsy guest breaks a piece off the fine china.
explanation.walkthrough: Spode is a brand of English bone china.
explanation.definitionFit: Spod is British slang for a dull, socially awkward person, a nerd ill at ease with others.

clue.text: Late addition after stodge: nasty stomach ache

indicators.note: this word puts the addition behind the stuffing word

blocks.note: to stodge is to stuff oneself with food, to cram
a postscript is added late to a letter

explanation.surface: Overeating heavy food late in the evening brings on a bad bellyache.
explanation.definitionFit: Cramps are painful spasms, and stomach cramps are a common kind of abdominal pain.

clue.text: Upper class requiring gossip about inherited estate

indicators.note: around: the gossip word wraps the class letter

blocks.note: U means upper class in British usage

explanation.surface: Posh people need gossip about who inherited the family estate.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a taluk was a hereditary estate, and later an administrative subdivision of a district.

clue.text: Protective covering for old horse, one pulling light carriage

blocks.note: first meaning: an archaic word for a horse's trappings
second meaning: a horse used to draw a trap

explanation.walkthrough: A trap is a light two-wheeled carriage, so the horse between its shafts can be named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word both as an old term for horse armour or caparison and for a horse kept for a trap.

clue.text: It's solidified in castings? liquefied it's all sop

indicators.note: melted down, so the letters flow into a new shape

explanation.surface: Something hardens in its moulds once melted, then it's all mush.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastisol is a liquid suspension of PVC in a plasticiser that gels into a solid when heated, used for moulded products.

clue.text: Heretic, a sailor imprisoned in punishment once

indicators.note: locked up inside, so these letters sit within the punishment word

blocks.note: pine is an obsolete word for punishment or suffering

explanation.surface: A heretic and a sailor are locked up as a punishment in olden times.
explanation.definitionFit: The Patarines were a medieval reforming movement, and the name came to be applied to heretics such as the Cathars.

clue.text: Oven joint ready for the table, right off

indicators.note: taken off, so the named letter is removed

blocks.note: a roast is a joint of cooked meat

explanation.surface: A joint from the oven is ready for serving, with the heat switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a type of oven.

clue.text: Cast roar terribly, not one acting? they're piercing in the theatre?

indicators.note: without one, so a single-letter word is dropped
done terribly, so the letters come out badly arranged

blocks.note: a means one, and is removed

explanation.surface: An actor roars badly while a stage show's critics are cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Trocars are sharp-pointed surgical instruments used to pierce body cavities, so surgeons use them in operating rooms.

clue.text: Prince, English, king's equal of old

blocks.note: regal means of or like a king

explanation.surface: A prince of England matches a king in rank of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Peregal is an archaic word for a peer or an equal in rank.

clue.text: Tons included in half of tote, not wholly

indicators.note: only half is kept, the rest is cut away
put inside, so the single letter goes within the other piece

blocks.note: the tote is the pari-mutuel betting system

explanation.surface: Tons of money went into the betting pool, but not all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The tote is a betting system pooling all stakes, also called the pari-mutuel; its first half is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Partim is Latin for 'in part', used in English for something that holds only partially.

clue.text: Poultice, say, one that sticks round opening of laceration

indicators.note: the sticker word goes around the single letter
the opening of a word is its very first letter

blocks.note: a paster is one who pastes

explanation.surface: A dressing that sticks on round a fresh cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal plaster is a dressing spread on the skin, and a poultice is one example.

clue.text: One hoarding rent in heart of newsroom

indicators.note: the torn word sits inside the central letters
the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: 'heart of' keeps the central pair of letters
rent as the past tense of rend: torn apart

explanation.surface: Someone keeps stashing paper in the middle of a newspaper office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' is not money paid for lodging but the past tense of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A storer is someone who stores things away, which is what a hoarder does.

clue.text: Lyle's partner showing his bit in putt at eighteen

indicators.note: a bit of the following words is on display, tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A golfer's playing partner shows his skill with a putt on the eighteenth green.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate & Lyle is the British sugar company formed by merging Henry Tate's and Abram Lyle's firms.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Tate was the business partner of Abram Lyle's firm in the sugar merger.

clue.text: The human race displaying minimum of trust in ethics

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the ethics word
the least amount that can be taken, a single letter from the front

blocks.note: 'minimum of' keeps the least part, its first letter

explanation.surface: Humanity shows little trust in moral principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortality can mean mortal beings collectively, that is mankind.

clue.text: Fond of sledging at the Gabba? Offhand after half-century

definitions.text: Fond of sledging at the Gabba?

indicators.note: the offhand word comes behind the numeral

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A batsman reaches fifty at the Gabba and becomes casual and mouthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sledging is verbal abuse of opponents in cricket; the Gabba is Brisbane's cricket ground, and lairy is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairy is Australian and British slang for flashy and aggressively cocky, the type to trash-talk opponents.

clue.text: Like Caesar, wretchedly tinged with gore, losing reign, undone?

indicators.note: the letters of the ruling word are lost from the fodder
the removed word is unpicked, so its letters go in any order
done wretchedly, so the letters are in a mess

blocks.note: these letters, in any order ('undone'), are removed

explanation.surface: Caesar, bloodied and stabbed, loses his rule and is undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undone' says the removed word need not appear in order, only its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Toged means wearing a toga, the garment of a Roman citizen such as Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Series of actions: original cover featured in newspapers

indicators.note: appearing inside, so the abbreviation goes within the newspapers word

blocks.note: OC abbreviates original cover, a philatelic term

explanation.surface: A series of events shown in the papers, with the first front page.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is a sequence of steps taken to reach an end.

clue.text: Outsize bust? It must be held in for gym!

indicators.note: the answer is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A large bust needs holding in at the gym!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' is a drinking spree, not a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a spree or binge, and an orgy is a wild, excessive one.

clue.text: Nuclear device that's sunk mass in a dock

blocks.note: to bob is to dock or cut short, as a tail or hair

explanation.definitionFit: An A-bomb is an atomic bomb, a weapon powered by nuclear fission.

clue.text: Lute string? note position when it's plucked

explanation.definitionFit: Mese was the middle string or note of the Greek lyre system, so a string of a plucked instrument.

clue.text: Exhausted fellow in rush: what'll cab in Wellington charge?

clue.text: Generation with little energy straying off the straight

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for energy

clue.text: Range adapted highly for the art of carving

clue.text: End of spinney? Sadder to see rotting round such forest trees

indicators.note: rotting things decay and break down out of shape
the scrambled letters go around the single letter
